newsitem.title: JAPAN: DDI, IDO announce cellular phone business tie-up.
newsitem.headline: DDI, IDO announce cellular phone business tie-up.

text.p: Japanese long-distance carriers DDI Corp and IDO Corp, an affiliate of Toyota Motor Corp, announced on Wednesday that they will jointly introduce a new digital cell phone service in Japan beginning in April 1998 under the same brand name.
But the two firms ruled out the possibility of developing their cooperation into a broader alliance involving capital, personnel and marketing.
"It is difficult to discuss a merger without considering a difference in business culture," IDO president Takeo Tsukada told a news conference.

The two companies also said they have selected Motorola Inc of the United States as a system integrator for their seamless CDMA (code division multiple access) next-generation digital cellular phone system.
They said they had placed an order with Motorola for an exchange system but did not disclose the value of the order.
The two companies said their capital investment in the new service would total 300 billion yen, which they would provide roughly equally.
